Review profile: general

Task: Review this change for correctness, regressions, API design, missing tests, maintainability, and user-facing behavior changes. Return only real, actionable defects with concrete evidence and an exact code pointer. No praise, summaries, speculation, style preferences, or nice-to-have refactors.

Output format:
- Start with one verdict line: approve / approve with nits / request changes, plus a short reason.
- Then list actionable findings only. Each finding MUST be a separate top-level Markdown bullet starting with [high], [medium], or [low].
- Include an exact file:line pointer in each finding when possible, plus the bug, impact, and fix in one concise paragraph.
- Do not combine multiple defects in one bullet or paragraph. Do not emit severity-heading paragraphs like "**[HIGH] ...**" without a leading bullet.
- If there are no actionable findings, output only the verdict line.

Scope: review the commits unique to this branch vs origin/HEAD, plus any uncommitted changes in the working tree. Ignore code outside this scope.

  65bd6f32 Claude Code (touched: 16 files) prompt: create test data in `/Users/ninawork/entire/devenv/importtest` for me to import with sample agent sessions to import`

`/simplify → 4 cleanup agents in parallel → apply the fixes`

You are improving the quality of the changed code, not hunting for bugs. Review
it for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude issues, then fix what you
find. Do not look for correctness bugs — that is what `/code-review` is for.

## Phase 0 — Gather the diff

Run `git diff @{upstream}...HEAD` (or `git diff main...HEAD` / `git diff HEAD~1`
if there's no upstream) to get the unified diff under review. If there are
uncommitted changes, or the range diff is empty, also run `git diff HEAD` and
include the working-tree changes in scope — the review often runs before the
commit. If a PR number, branch name, or file path was passed as an argument,
review that target instead. Treat this diff as the review scope.

## Phase 1 — Review (4 cleanup agents in parallel)

Launch **4 independent review agents** via the Agent tool, all in a
single message so they run concurrently. Pass each agent the diff and one of
the four angles below. Each returns its findings with `file`, `line`, a
one-line `summary`, and the concrete cost (what is duplicated, wasted, or
harder to maintain).

### Reuse

Flag new code that re-implements something the codebase
already has — Grep shared/utility modules and files adjacent to the change,
and name the existing helper to call instead.

### Simplification

Flag unnecessary complexity the diff adds: redundant or derivable state,
copy-paste with slight variation, deep nesting, dead code left behind. Name
the simpler form that does the same job.

### Efficiency

Flag wasted work the diff introduces: redundant computation or repeated I/O,
independent operations run sequentially, blocking work added to startup or
hot paths. Also flag long-lived objects built from closures or captured
environments — they keep the entire enclosing scope alive for the object's
lifetime (a memory leak when that scope holds large values); prefer a
class/struct that copies only the fields it needs. Name the cheaper
alternative.

### Altitude

Check that each change is implemented at the right depth, not as a fragile
bandaid. Special cases layered on shared infrastructure are a sign the fix
isn't deep enough — prefer generalizing the underlying mechanism over adding
special cases.

## Phase 2 — Apply the fixes

Wait for all four agents to complete, dedup findings that point at the same
line or mechanism, and fix each remaining one directly. Skip any finding whose
fix would change intended behavior, require changes well outside the reviewed
diff, or that you judge to be a false positive — note the skip rather than
arguing with it. Finish with a brief summary of what was fixed and what was
skipped (or confirm the code was already clean).

1	// Package agentimport imports a coding agent's pre-existing local transcripts
2	// into Entire as read-only, commit-less checkpoints on the v1 metadata branch.
3	//
4	// The orchestration (discovery loop, idempotent per-turn IDs, redaction, and
5	// the checkpoint write) is agent-agnostic and lives here. Each agent plugs in
6	// an Importer that knows where its transcripts live and how to split one into
7	// per-user-prompt turns. Claude Code is the only implementation today
8	// (see claude.go); others register themselves the same way.
9	package agentimport
10	
11	import (
12		"context"
13		"crypto/sha256"
14		"encoding/hex"
15		"fmt"
16		"os"
17		"sort"
18		"time"
19	
20		"github.com/go-git/go-git/v6"
21	
22		"github.com/entireio/cli/cmd/entire/cli/agent/types"
23		cp "github.com/entireio/cli/cmd/entire/cli/checkpoint"
24		"github.com/entireio/cli/cmd/entire/cli/checkpoint/id"
25		"github.com/entireio/cli/cmd/entire/cli/session"
26		"github.com/entireio/cli/redact"
27	)
28	
29	// LookbackDays bounds how far back import reaches. Fixed this pass (no flag).
30	const LookbackDays = 30
31	
32	// SessionFile is one discovered agent transcript for a repo.
33	type SessionFile struct {
34		Path      string // absolute path to the transcript file
35		SessionID string // agent session id (used in checkpoint metadata)
36	}
37	
38	// Turn is one user-prompt turn extracted from a session transcript. Line
39	// offsets are in raw-line space (newline-counted), matching transcript slicing
40	// and the agent token-usage helpers.
41	type Turn struct {
42		LineStart, LineEnd int
43		UUID               string
44		Prompt, Model      string
45		CreatedAt          time.Time
46		Tokens             *types.TokenUsage
47	}
48	
49	// Importer is the per-agent seam: it locates an agent's transcripts for a repo
50	// and splits one into per-turn units. Everything else (idempotency, redaction,
51	// writing) is handled generically by Run.
52	type Importer interface {
53		// Name is the registry key and the provenance source (e.g. "claude-code").
54		Name() string
55		// AgentType is the display name stored in checkpoint metadata (e.g. "Claude Code").
56		AgentType() types.AgentType
57		// Discover returns the agent's transcript files for the repo within the
58		// lookback window. overridePath replaces the default transcript dir;
59		// sessionFilter, when non-empty, keeps only matching session IDs.
60		Discover(repoRoot, overridePath string, now time.Time, sessionFilter []string) ([]SessionFile, error)
61		// SplitTurns splits one session's raw transcript bytes into per-turn units.
62		SplitTurns(sf SessionFile, full []byte) ([]Turn, error)
63	}
64	
65	// importers is the static set of supported agents. Adding an agent is a new
66	// Importer implementation appended here — no init() / runtime registration.
67	var importers = []Importer{
68		claudeImporter{},
69		cursorImporter{},
70		piImporter{},
71		factoryImporter{},
72		codexImporter{},
73		copilotImporter{},
74		geminiImporter{},
75	}
76	
77	// Get returns the importer registered under name.
78	//
79	//nolint:ireturn // Importer is the intended polymorphic seam returned to callers.
80	func Get(name string) (Importer, bool) {
81		for _, imp := range importers {
82			if imp.Name() == name {
83				return imp, true
84			}
85		}
86		return nil, false
87	}
88	
89	// All returns every supported importer, sorted by name.
90	func All() []Importer {
91		out := append([]Importer(nil), importers...)
92		sort.Slice(out, func(i, j int) bool { return out[i].Name() < out[j].Name() })
93		return out
94	}
95	
96	// Options configures an import run.
97	type Options struct {
98		RepoRoot      string
99		OverridePath  string
100		SessionFilter []string
101		Now           time.Time
102		DryRun        bool
103	}
104	
105	// Result summarizes an import run.
106	type Result struct {
107		SessionsScanned int
108		TurnsImported   int
109		TurnsSkipped    int
110	}
111	
112	// DeriveCheckpointID produces a stable 12-hex checkpoint ID for an imported
113	// turn. Re-importing the same (sessionID, turnUUID) yields the same ID, which
114	// is how import stays idempotent.
115	func DeriveCheckpointID(sessionID, turnUUID string) id.CheckpointID {
116		sum := sha256.Sum256([]byte(sessionID + "/" + turnUUID))
117		return id.MustCheckpointID(hex.EncodeToString(sum[:6])) // 6 bytes = 12 lowercase hex chars
118	}
119	
120	// Run imports the given agent's transcripts (within the lookback window) as
121	// read-only checkpoints on the v1 metadata branch (Kind "imported"). It is
122	// idempotent: turns whose deterministic ID already exists are skipped.
123	func Run(ctx context.Context, repo *git.Repository, imp Importer, opts Options) (Result, error) {
124		var res Result
125		files, err := imp.Discover(opts.RepoRoot, opts.OverridePath, opts.Now, opts.SessionFilter)
126		if err != nil {
127			return res, fmt.Errorf("discover %s sessions: %w", imp.Name(), err)
128		}
129	
130		stores, err := cp.Open(ctx, repo, cp.OpenOptions{})
131		if err != nil {
132			return res, fmt.Errorf("open checkpoint store: %w", err)
133		}
134		existing := make(map[string]bool)
135		if infos, listErr := stores.Persistent.List(ctx); listErr == nil {
136			for _, in := range infos {
137				existing[in.CheckpointID.String()] = true
138			}
139		}
140	
141		for _, sf := range files {
142			res.SessionsScanned++
143			full, readErr := os.ReadFile(sf.Path)
144			if readErr != nil {
145				return res, fmt.Errorf("read %s: %w", sf.Path, readErr)
146			}
147			turns, splitErr := imp.SplitTurns(sf, full)
148			if splitErr != nil {
149				return res, fmt.Errorf("split %s session %s: %w", imp.Name(), sf.SessionID, splitErr)
150			}
151			// Redact the session transcript once and reuse it for every turn's
152			// checkpoint (each turn stores the full session transcript with its own
153			// CheckpointTranscriptStart). Redacting per turn would be O(turns).
154			// Computed lazily so a fully-skipped or dry-run file pays nothing.
155			var red redact.RedactedBytes
156			redacted := false
157			for _, turn := range turns {
158				cid := DeriveCheckpointID(sf.SessionID, turn.UUID)
159				if existing[cid.String()] {
160					res.TurnsSkipped++
161					continue
162				}
163				if opts.DryRun {
164					res.TurnsImported++ // counts what would import
165					continue
166				}
167				if !redacted {
168					r, rerr := redact.JSONLBytes(full)
169					if rerr != nil {
170						return res, fmt.Errorf("redact %s transcript: %w", sf.SessionID, rerr)
171					}
172					red = r
173					redacted = true
174				}
175				if err := writeTurn(ctx, stores, imp, cid, sf, red, turn); err != nil {
176					return res, err
177				}
178				existing[cid.String()] = true
179				res.TurnsImported++
180			}
181		}
182		return res, nil
183	}
184	
185	func writeTurn(ctx context.Context, stores *cp.Stores, imp Importer, cid id.CheckpointID, sf SessionFile, red redact.RedactedBytes, turn Turn) error {
186		if err := stores.Persistent.Write(ctx, cp.Session(cp.WriteOptions{
187			CheckpointID:              cid,
188			SessionID:                 sf.SessionID,
189			CreatedAt:                 turn.CreatedAt,
190			Strategy:                  "import",
191			Kind:                      string(session.KindImported),
192			Agent:                     imp.AgentType(),
193			Model:                     turn.Model,
194			Transcript:                red,
195			Prompts:                   []string{turn.Prompt},
196			CheckpointsCount:          1,
197			CheckpointTranscriptStart: turn.LineStart,
198			TokenUsage:                turn.Tokens,
199		})); err != nil {
200			return fmt.Errorf("write imported checkpoint %s: %w", cid, err)
201		}
202		return nil
203	}

All four agents have reported. Let me synthesize and dedup the findings before applying.

**Convergent findings:**
- **Double prompt-predicate call** (efficiency + simplification): `pi/factory/codex/copilot` call `*PromptText` once to detect a turn start and again inside the loop to recover the prompt — redundant re-parse of the same line, and the `, _ :=` discard is a smell.
- **Timestamp parse-or-zero idiom** (simplification): the `time.Parse(...); if err { ts = time.Time{} }` block is copy-pasted in `cursor/pi/copilot`, and `codex.go` already has `codexLineTime` doing the same thing — extract one helper.
- **Big `Discover`/`SplitTurns` helper extraction** (reuse + altitude): real, but spans out-of-scope `claude.go` and requires reconciling divergent token-calc signatures — large/risky.
- **O(turns²) `joinLines`** (efficiency): real, but pre-existing in `claude.go` and needs agent token-calc API changes.
- **cursor.go:58 `os.Stat` vs `e.Info()`**: false positive — `path` may be a *nested* file (`<dir>/<id>/<id>.jsonl`) where `e` is the directory, so `e.Info()` would stat the wrong thing.

I'll apply the two safe, contained wins (double-predicate + timestamp helper), and skip the large structural refactor and the cross-package efficiency change. Let me make the edits.

content.text:
All ten edits are staged but blocked pending write permission — please approve them. Here's what I'm applying and what I deliberately skipped.

## Applied (behavior-preserving cleanups)

**1. Shared `parseRFC3339OrZero` helper** (`agentimport.go`, new) — replaces the copy-pasted `time.Parse(...); if err { ts = time.Time{} }` idiom in `cursor.go`, `pi.go`, `copilot.go`, and collapses the parse tail of `codex.go`'s `codexLineTime`. Four duplicated blocks → one helper.

**2. Shared `turnStart` type + single-pass prompt capture** (`agentimport.go`, new type; applied in `pi.go`, `factory.go`, `codex.go`, `copilot.go`) — each importer was calling its `*PromptText(rawLines[start])` predicate a *second* time inside the turn loop, re-unmarshalling the line just to recover the prompt it already matched during start detection. Now the prompt is captured once at detection (`turnStart{line, prompt}`) and reused. Removes the redundant parse and the `prompt, _ :=` discard smell.

Net: ~30 lines removed, no behavior change (same prompt value, same timestamp).

## Skipped (with reasons)

- **Big `Discover`/`SplitTurns` helper extraction** (reuse + altitude agents, "worth doing now") — the deepest finding, but a clean version must pull in out-of-scope `claude.go` and reconcile genuinely divergent token-calc signatures (claude/factory take `subagentsDir`; pi/codex/copilot don't; cursor takes none; gemini is whole-session). That's a real design change, not a behavior-preserving cleanup — better as its own reviewed PR than folded into this one.
- **O(turns²) `joinLines(rawLines[:end])`** (efficiency agent) — real, but the same pattern is pre-existing in `claude.go` and the fix requires changing the agents' token-calc APIs (well outside this diff).
- **`cursor.go:58` `os.Stat` → `e.Info()`** (efficiency agent) — false positive: in the nested layout `path` is `<dir>/<id>/<id>.jsonl` while `e` is the *directory*, so `e.Info()` would stat the wrong inode.
- **`sortSessionFiles` 1-line helper** (reuse agent) — marginal; extracting a one-line `slices.SortFunc` call adds indirection for negligible gain.

Once you approve the edits, I'll run `mise run fmt && mise run lint` and the `agentimport` package tests to confirm nothing broke.
